description:
## Problem
On #4463 (run 45113582370, job 137491683967) `windows-tests (windows-latest, py3.12)` printed 94% at 04:53:57Z and nothing more until the 30-minute job limit cancelled it at 05:15:44Z. The lane runs `--timeout=120` with the thread method, which never fired or named a test. The likely cause was new tests launching `uv run` children with no subprocess timeout; after 5111fb2e3a added timeouts and used the current interpreter, the job passed in 6 min 33 s (run 45262079148). The cause is inferred, not reproduced. `scripts/check_windows_antipatterns.py` has no rule for subprocess calls in tests without `timeout=`.

## Change
First reproduce: a test whose child sleeps past the limit on `windows-latest` under the lane's pytest-timeout settings, recording whether the test is named. Then choose one: a ratchet rule rejecting new `subprocess` calls without `timeout=` under `tests/`, with the existing count as baseline; or a lane setting that names the hung test before the job limit.

## Decision gates
- Choose the approach after the reproduction, and record why.
- A ratchet must not fail existing code (baseline count). Changing the lane's timeout values needs the owner.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the reproduction run and its outcome are linked; and either a fixture test shows the ratchet rejects a new untimed child, or an induced hang on `windows-latest` names the test within the job limit.

## Guardrails
- Work in a linked worktree from `make worktree-create`; never write in the primary clone. Stage named paths only; commit as the pinned human identity with no agent attribution.
- Push only after `make pr-preflight` passes on the exact head. Never `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite authorship.
- Arm only with `make pr-arm`, once per head. A second attempt only when the refusal named a cause that is now fixed; a third needs the owner. `make pr-rerun` only for a job the runner cancelled or never ran, never to re-roll a failed test.
- Never post a stand-in review. Resolve a review thread only after the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again.
- Heavy work only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking target. Never set `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force`, `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK` or `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off`.
- Any new limit, threshold, default or user-facing label is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- Do not mark a test skip, xfail, quarantine or slow to make it pass.
- Report only what merged and what was verified, with run ids and heads.
